stimuli.description: Modular noise barriers with panels that could be reversed to present either an absorptive or reflective face to traffic. Measurements taken at two sites: a single 3m high barrier on an eight-lane motorway, and 3.7m high parallel barriers on a dual carriageway in a shallow cutting.

limitations: The effect of traffic stream in screening sound reflected from the farside barrier was not fully accounted for by prediction models.
The assumption of vehicle width and angle of incidence in calculations may slightly underestimate the degree of screening of reflected sound.
The effects of vehicle speed on source strength were not taken into account.
Simplified geometry assumed in the prediction model (e.g., presence of safety fences, reflective ground beams, limited barrier length and curvature) may have reduced recorded noise level increases.
The sides of many large vehicles may not provide conditions for specular reflections, affecting multiple reflections between vehicle and barrier.
Less than perfect absorption and reflective properties of barrier panel faces may have slightly reduced noise level increases.

Scattering by the vehicle stream and associated turbulence, and simplified geometries and acoustic performances of barrier panels assumed in models contribute to discrepancies between measured and predicted levels.
Further carefully controlled field studies with varying traffic flows are required to fully quantify these effects.
